topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the lecture by outlining learning outcomes and setting up key concepts in cancer evolution and the tumor microenvironment.

topics.label: Clonal Evolution and Epigenetic Plasticity in Tumor Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer develops through Darwinian natural selection of advantageous mutations alongside non-mutational epigenetic alterations that modify gene expression.

topics.label: Cell of Origin and Cancer Stem Cell Hierarchies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore whether cancers initiate and propagate from tissue-specific stem cells or differentiated progenitor cells through hierarchical and stochastic models.

topics.label: Microenvironmental Signals and Inflammation in Tumor Promotion and Growth
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how external environmental promoters, chronic inflammation, and stromal codependency provide the permissive microenvironment required for tumor initiation, malignant progression, and maintenance.

topics.label: Technologies for Mapping Tumor Evolution and Microenvironments
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the experimental sequencing, spatial transcriptomic, and proteomic tools used to interrogate clonal history and tumor-microenvironment interactions.

topics.label: Integrated Synthesis of Cancer Evolution Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes the lecture's core themes into a unified evolutionary model where genetic mutations, cell-of-origin properties, epigenetic plasticity, and microenvironmental coevolution converge to permit malignancy.

topics.label: Conclusion and Next Lecture Preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and previews the upcoming lecture on cancer therapy.
